newsitem.title: UK: UK's OFT plans to curb BA /AA deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK's OFT plans to curb BA /AA deal - paper.

text.p: Britain's Office of Fair Trading plans to impose curbs on British Airways Plc's proposed alliance with American Airlines as a condition for not referring it to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, the Times said.

Airline sources told the newspaper the two airlines would be required to reduce their combined number of slots at London's Heathrow airport which, together with those belonging to BA's partner airlines, is close to 50 percent of the total.
A spokesman for the OFT, speaking by telephone, said the report was speculation.

The organisation's director general has yet to advise Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang whether or not he feels the deal should be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. The Times said the OFT also wanted concessions on terminal and airport capacity from the two airlines so rival carriers had sufficient gates and parking facilities.

The two would also have to allow frequent flyer points earned on their flights to book flights on other airlines, not just their own. The OFT planned to restrict the use by the two airlines of discounts for travel agents and concessions for regular corporate travellers, known as fidelity rebates.
BA and American's plans have attracted fierce criticism from rival airlines as well as consumer groups who say the alliance will dominate the London transatlantic market.

Under the alliance, BA intends to coordinate its 244 flights a week from Britain to 22 U.S. destinations with all of American's 238 flights a week from seven U.S. airports to 12 European destinations.

BA and American say the deal will lead to greater competition on transatlantic routes because it will only go ahead if Britain and the U.S. liberalise the market with an "open skies" trade pact. But "open skies" talks between government negotiators broke down last month.
